To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the systematical, clustered, nested sampling design can be used for the collection of field observations to match the image pixel size for mapping forest carbon stocks and the accuracy assessment.
a systematic, nested and clustering design can be used to collect field data at multiple spatial resolutions and to map carbon density at multiple resolutions using remote sensing data.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) Can we use a systematical, clustered, nested sampling design to collect field data for mapping forest carbon at multiple spatial resolutions and conduct accuracy assessment?
the development of a new sampling design for mapping and accuracy assessment at different spatial resolution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed methodological framework provided the potential to map forest carbon stock at multiple spatial resolutions with a high accuracy.
the study provides a new methodology to map forest carbon at different scales using a combination of sample plot and image information.

the systematical, nesting and clustering sampling design provides the potential to formulate an efficient methodological framework to combine sample plot and image information to map forest carbon densities and conduct accuracy assessment for multiple spatial resolutions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the systematical, nesting and clustering sampling design is an effective method to obtain the reference dataset at multiple spatial resolutions for mapping forest carbon densities.

the systematical, clustered and nested sampling design provided the possibility to obtain spatial information on forest carbon density at various spatial resolutions, while the combination of Landsat images, SGCSWA, and the sampling design resulted in the highest accuracy in mapping forest carbon density at a 500 m spatial resolution.

the systematical, nesting and clustering sampling design provides the potential to obtain reference values for mapping and accuracy assessment at multiple resolutions and that the combinations of SGCSWA or SBGCS with Landsat images provide the potential to map forest carbon densities at multiple spatial resolutions with high accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have demonstrated the potential to combine a nested and clustering sampling with a multi-resolution mapping to map forest carbon stock.
the systematical, nesting, and clustering sampling design can provide a framework to map forest C density at multiple spatial resolution.
the combination of SGCSWA, SGBCS, and Landsat 8 can be used for upscaling forest carbon density from 30 m to 250 m, 500 m and 1000m spatial resolutions.
